paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God brings together what got split apart. Israel had been torn into two kingdoms, and God told Ezekiel to hold two sticks and join them into one, so that they "become one in your hand" (Ezekiel 37:17). Then God said it plainly: "I will make them into a single stick, and they will become one in My hand" (Ezekiel 37:19). Notice whose hand it is. Ezekiel only holds the sticks, but God is the One who does the joining.

So what do the exiles get? A promise bigger than a reunion. God says He will gather them, cleanse them, and give them "one shepherd for all of them" (Ezekiel 37:24). He says He will make "a covenant of peace with them" (Ezekiel 37:26), and that His dwelling place will be with them. Then comes the line that holds it all together: "I will be their God, and they will be My people" (Ezekiel 37:27).

Here's why that matters to you, baker. Maybe you've got something in your life that feels cracked in two, and you can't see how it ever gets fixed. This passage says the God who holds the sticks can also hold the pieces of your life. I spent years in a drawer thinking nobody was coming, and I'm telling you, the One who gathers is good at it. This is the kind of promise that keeps my ovens warm.
